errata.original_assessment: MediaDive2234 uses2.3 g EMJH base,1.5 g agarose,900 ml water and100 ml enrichment. Enrichment is added after basal sterilization/cooling; it is neither base nor complete medium.
errata.corrected_assessment: MediaDive solution2234, named Main sol.1113 and belonging to DSMZ medium1113, uses 2.3 g EMJH base, 1.5 g agarose, 900 mL water and 100 mL enrichment. Enrichment is added after basal sterilization and cooling; it is neither the base nor the complete medium. The number2234 is a solution identifier, not the medium number.

errata.original_assessment: CHEBI86465 is potassium aluminium sulfate dodecahydrate with twelve waters. It cannot correct NBRC1126 literal two-water source merely by similarity.
errata.corrected_assessment: CHEBI:86465 is potassium aluminium sulfate dodecahydrate with twelve waters. The two-water spelling belongs to the frozen/provider representation; the actual NBRC1126 recipe prints KAl(SO4)2·12H2O at0.018 g in its one-litre trace-element solution. That original recipe supports the occurrence-specific correction to the existing dodecahydrate owner; this conclusion is not inferred from ontology-name similarity. Preserve the malformed spelling as correction provenance, not a new dihydrate identity or globally resolving alias. Full-owner inherited obligations remain.

errata.original_assessment: JCM448 prints Mg(NO3)·6H2O, while its GMO annotation claims magnesium nitrate hexahydrate. Missing nitrate stoichiometry is not corrected by a metadata label; the real source-form ambiguity remains.
errata.corrected_assessment: The TOGO M449 provider component_name is Mg(NO3)·6H2O and its GMO annotation names magnesium nitrate hexahydrate. The original JCM448 recipe instead prints Mg(NO3)2·6H2O at2.54 g. That original recipe resolves the missing nitrate coefficient for the assigned occurrence and supports the existing CAS13446-18-9 hexahydrate owner, consistently with sealed case129. This is an occurrence-specific source correction, not a correction inferred from the metadata label alone. Preserve the malformed provider/frozen spelling as provenance; do not invent a remaining source-form ambiguity or assert exact anhydrous identity.

errata.original_assessment: NBRC1126 trace recipe prints KAl(SO4)2·2H2O. A twelve-water ontology comparator does not establish a correction; no dodecahydrate source binding is justified.
errata.corrected_assessment: The TOGO M1882 provider component_name is KAl(SO4)2·2H2O, matching the frozen malformed spelling. The original NBRC1126 trace-element recipe prints KAl(SO4)2·12H2O at0.018 g per one-litre trace batch. The original recipe therefore supports the occurrence-specific dodecahydrate correction and existing owner, consistently with sealed case66; it is stronger evidence than similarity to an ontology comparator. Retain the provider error as correction provenance and preserve the remaining full-owner obligations.

errata.original_reasoning: Both JCM621 and1066 literally state 0.2% Fe(NH4)SO4 in0.037% HCl. A source-qualified stock with an unresolved malformed iron component is supported. The chemically explicit JCM764 Mohr stock is a comparator, not proof that these printed formulas are equivalent. Both percentage bases and solvent remain unknown.
errata.corrected_reasoning: Both original JCM621 and JCM1066 recipes print 0.2% Fe(NH4)2(SO4)·6H2O in0.037% HCl. The printed expression contains two ammonium groups and six waters but lacks the second sulfate coefficient required for the ordinary Mohr formula. A source-qualified partial stock with that unresolved iron component remains supported. The chemically explicit JCM764 Mohr stock is a comparator, not proof that the malformed source expressions can be silently corrected. Both percentage bases and solvent remain unspecified.
